subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Parallelograms, Rhombuses and Trapeziums: Properties and Unknown Angles
seo_title: P5 Parallelogram, Rhombus and Trapezium Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Properties of parallelogram, rhombus and trapezium; finding unknown angles
meta_desc: Free P5 practice: name parallelograms, rhombuses and trapeziums, use their properties and find unknown angles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal and angles next to each other add up to 180°.
key_sub: ∠A = 64°, so ∠B = 180° − 64° = 116° and ∠C = 64°. In a trapezium, the 2 angles on a slanted side add up to 180°.
body_html:
Parallelogram, rhombus and trapezium

Arrows show parallel sides. Tick marks show equal sides. Name a figure by what it must have.

FigureSidesAngles
Parallelogram2 pairs of parallel sides; opposite sides are equalOpposite angles are equal
RhombusA parallelogram with 4 equal sidesOpposite angles are equal
SquareA rhombus with 4 right anglesAll 4 angles are 90°
TrapeziumExactly 1 pair of parallel sidesThe 2 angles on each slanted side add up to 180°

Angles in a parallelogram and a rhombus

Opposite angles are equal. Angles next to each other add up to 180°. All 4 angles add up to 360°.

Example 1

ABCD is a parallelogram and ∠A = 64°. Find ∠B and ∠C.

∠B is next to ∠A: ∠B = 180° − 64° = 116°. ∠C is opposite ∠A, so ∠C = 64°.

Answer: ∠B = 116°, ∠C = 64°

Angles in a trapezium

Find the parallel sides first. The 2 angles at the ends of each slanted side lie between the parallel sides, so they add up to 180°. Opposite angles of a trapezium are usually not equal.

Example 2

ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC. ∠B = 48°. Find ∠C.

∠B and ∠C are at the ends of side BC, between the parallel sides. ∠C = 180° − 48°.

Answer: 132°

Figures with triangles

Use the facts one step at a time: the angles of a triangle add up to 180°, angles on a straight line add up to 180°, and an isosceles triangle has 2 equal angles.

Example 3

ABCD is a rhombus and ∠A = 64°. Find ∠x = ∠ABD.

Triangle ABD is isosceles, so ∠ABD = ∠ADB. ∠x = (180° − 64°) ÷ 2 = 116° ÷ 2.

Answer: 58°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Opposite angles of a parallelogram add up to 180°Opposite angles are equal. Angles next to each other add up to 180°
A trapezium has 2 pairs of parallel sidesA trapezium has exactly 1 pair. 2 pairs make a parallelogram
A rhombus must have right angles, like a squareA rhombus needs only 4 equal sides. A square is a rhombus with right angles
In a trapezium, ∠A + ∠B = 180°Add the 2 angles on the same slanted side, such as ∠A + ∠D when AB ∥ DC
Writing 360° − the given angleUse 180° for angles next to each other, and 360° only for all 4 angles

faq.q: What is taught about parallelograms, rhombuses and trapeziums in P5?
faq.a: Primary 5 students learn the properties of a parallelogram, a rhombus and a trapezium, and use them to find unknown angles, including in figures made with triangles.
Yes. A rhombus is a parallelogram with 4 equal sides, and a square has 4 equal sides, so a square is a rhombus with 4 right angles.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with angles in a parallelogram?
faq.a: Thinking that opposite angles add up to 180°. Opposite angles are equal; it is the angles next to each other that add up to 180°.

faq.q: Is this topic in the MOE syllabus for Primary 5?
faq.a: Yes. Properties of the parallelogram, rhombus and trapezium and finding unknown angles are Primary 5 Geometry in the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus, and angle questions like these also appear in the PSLE.

items.q: Which figure is NOT a parallelogram?
items.e: Figure D has only 1 pair of parallel sides, so it is a trapezium, not a parallelogram. A rhombus and a rectangle are special parallelograms.

items.q: Which figure has 4 equal sides but no right angles?
items.e: Figure C is a rhombus: 4 equal sides and no right angles. The square also has 4 equal sides, but it has 4 right angles.

items.q: What is the best name for this figure? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezium.

items.q: What is the best name for this figure? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
items.e: Both pairs of opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel: 2 pairs.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. Is it a rhombus?
items.e: It has 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. With 4 right angles it is a special rhombus called a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this figure? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. The sides are not all equal and there are no right angles, so it is not a rhombus or a rectangle.

items.q: Which statement about a square is true?
c: It is a rhombus with 4 right angles
It has 1 pair of parallel sides
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides (so it is a rhombus) and 4 right angles. It has 2 pairs of parallel sides.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 2 pairs of parallel sides. Its sides are not all equal and it has no right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 2 pairs of parallel sides make a parallelogram. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus or a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this figure? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezium. Turning a figure does not change its name.

items.q: Siti says, “A trapezium has 2 pairs of parallel sides.” Is she right?
c: Yes, if its sides are equal
No, it has no parallel sides
items.e: A trapezium has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. A quadrilateral with 2 pairs is a parallelogram.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a trapezium have?
items.e: A trapezium has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. A figure with 2 pairs is a parallelogram.

items.q: What is the best name for this figure? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezium. Turning a figure does not change its name.

items.q: A rhombus is a parallelogram with ______.
items.e: A rhombus has 2 pairs of parallel sides like every parallelogram, and all 4 of its sides are equal. It does not need right angles; that would make it a square.

items.q: Which of these is always a parallelogram?
items.e: A rhombus has 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is always a parallelogram. A trapezium has only 1 pair.

items.q: What is the best name for this figure? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezium.

items.q: What is the best name for this figure? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square. Turning a figure does not change its name.

items.q: Which figure is a trapezium?
items.e: Figure B has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides (one set of arrows), so it is a trapezium. The other figures have 2 pairs of parallel sides.

items.q: What is the best name for this figure? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. The sides are not all equal and there are no right angles, so it is not a rhombus or a rectangle. Turning a figure does not change its name.

items.q: Which figure is a rhombus?
items.e: Figure A has 4 equal sides (tick marks on every side), so it is a rhombus. The parallelogram and the rectangle have only opposite sides equal.

sets.title: Properties: equal sides, equal angles and angles that add up to 180°

items.q: The perimeter of a rhombus is 52 cm. Find the length of one side.
items.e: A rhombus has 4 equal sides. One side = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm.

items.q: Which property does a rhombus have that a parallelogram does not always have?
items.e: Every parallelogram has parallel and equal opposite sides and equal opposite angles. Only a rhombus must have all 4 sides equal.

items.q: What do the 4 angles of any quadrilateral add up to?
items.e: A quadrilateral can be cut into 2 triangles along a diagonal. 2 × 180° = 360°.

items.q: Which property does a parallelogram have that a trapezium does not?
items.e: A trapezium has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. A parallelogram has 2 pairs.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. AB = 8 cm. Find its perimeter.
items.e: All 4 sides of a rhombus are equal. Perimeter = 4 × 8 = 32 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠DAB and ∠x lie between the parallel sides AB and DC, on the same side AD, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 105° = 75°.

items.q: PQRS is a trapezium. PQ ∥ SR and ∠P = 80°. Which angle must be 100°?
items.e: ∠P and ∠S are at the two ends of side PS, between the parallel sides PQ and SR. They add up to 180°, so ∠S = 180° − 80° = 100°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = 9 cm and AD = 5 cm. Find its perimeter.
items.e: Opposite sides are equal, so the sides are 9 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm and 5 cm. Perimeter = 9 + 5 + 9 + 5 = 28 cm.

items.q: Which is true about every rhombus?
c: All sides equal, opposite angles equal
Only 1 pair of sides is parallel
items.e: A rhombus has 4 equal sides and, like every parallelogram, equal opposite angles. All 4 angles are equal only in a square.

items.q: Which is true about the opposite angles of a parallelogram?
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. It is the angles next to each other that add up to 180°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A + ∠C = 150°. Find ∠B.
items.e: ∠A and ∠C are opposite, so they are equal: ∠A = 150° ÷ 2 = 75°. ∠B is next to ∠A, so ∠B = 180° − 75° = 105°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠ABC and ∠x lie between the parallel sides AB and DC, on the same side BC, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 48° = 132°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB = 12 cm and BC = 7 cm. Find the length of CD.
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal. CD is opposite AB, so CD = 12 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. ∠x is opposite ∠DAB, so ∠x = 64°.

items.q: PQRS is a parallelogram. PQ = 15 cm and its perimeter is 46 cm. Find the length of QR.
items.e: PQ + QR is half the perimeter: 46 ÷ 2 = 23 cm. QR = 23 − 15 = 8 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Which two angles are equal?
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. ∠B and ∠D are opposite each other. Angles next to each other, such as ∠A and ∠B, add up to 180°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠x.
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so angles next to each other add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 124° = 56°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. ∠x is opposite ∠ABC, so ∠x = 118°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠x and ∠DAB are next to each other, between the parallel sides AD and BC, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 72° = 108°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Which two angles must add up to 180°?
items.e: ∠A and ∠D are at the two ends of side AD, between the parallel sides AB and DC, so they add up to 180°. ∠A and ∠B are on the same parallel side, so they do not.

sets.title: Unknown angles in parallelograms and rhombuses

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. ABE is a straight line. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠ABC = 180° − 65° = 115° (angles next to each other). ABE is a straight line, so ∠x = 180° − 115° = 65°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A is twice as large as ∠B. Find ∠A.
items.e: ∠A and ∠B are next to each other, so they add up to 180°. 3 units = 180°, 1 unit = 60°. ∠A = 2 units = 120°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠x and ∠BCD are next to each other, on side DC, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 47° = 133°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. ABE is a straight line. Find ∠x.
items.e: ABE is a straight line, so ∠ABC = 180° − 52° = 128°. ∠x is opposite ∠ABC, so ∠x = 128°.

items.q: In parallelogram PQRS, ∠P = 57°. Find ∠Q + ∠R.
In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A is 30° more than ∠B. Find ∠A.
ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠DAB and ∠x are next to each other, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 58° = 122°.

items.q: PQRS is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠PSR and ∠x are next to each other, on side SR, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 113° = 67°.

items.q: Three angles of a parallelogram are 71°, 109° and 71°. Find the fourth angle.
items.e: The 4 angles add up to 360°: 360° − 71° − 109° − 71° = 109°. It is opposite the other 109° angle.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A + ∠C = 136°. Find ∠D.
items.e: ∠A and ∠C are opposite, so ∠A = 136° ÷ 2 = 68°. ∠D is next to ∠A: ∠D = 180° − 68° = 112°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x + ∠y.
ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠x.
items.e: Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal. ∠x is opposite ∠DAB, so ∠x = 76°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. DCE is a straight line. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠BCD = 180° − 110° = 70° (angles next to each other). DCE is a straight line, so ∠x = 180° − 70° = 110°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. ADE is a straight line. Find ∠x.
items.e: ADE is a straight line, so ∠ADC = 180° − 71° = 109°. ∠x is opposite ∠ADC, so ∠x = 109°.

items.q: One angle of a rhombus is 38°. Find the largest angle of the rhombus.
items.e: Angles next to each other add up to 180°: 180° − 38° = 142°. The angles are 38°, 142°, 38° and 142°.

items.q: In rhombus ABCD, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 250°. Find ∠D.
items.e: The 4 angles add up to 360°, so ∠D = 360° − 250° = 110°. Check: ∠A = ∠C = 70° and ∠B = ∠D = 110°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠x and ∠ADC are opposite angles of the parallelogram, so they are equal. ∠x = 99°.

items.q: Two angles next to each other in a parallelogram differ by 40°. Find the larger angle.
items.e: The two angles add up to 180°. 180° − 40° = 140°, so the smaller angle is 140° ÷ 2 = 70°. The larger is 70° + 40° = 110°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠x and ∠ABC are next to each other, on side AB, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 77° = 103°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠x.
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so ∠DAB and ∠x add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 46° = 134°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠ABC and ∠x lie between the parallel sides, on side BC, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 57° = 123°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x + ∠y.
ABCD is a trapezium. AD ∥ BC. Find ∠x.
items.e: Here the parallel sides are AD and BC. ∠BCD and ∠x are on side CD, between them, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 120° = 60°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: AB and DC are the parallel sides, even when they stand up. ∠BCD and ∠x are on side BC, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 106° = 74°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. ∠A is 24° more than ∠D. Find ∠A.
The angles of a trapezium are 72°, 108°, 95° and ∠x. Find ∠x.
PQRS is a trapezium. PQ ∥ SR and ∠Q = 64°. Which of these must be true?
items.e: ∠Q and ∠R are at the two ends of side QR, between the parallel sides, so ∠R = 180° − 64° = 116°. We cannot find ∠P or ∠S from ∠Q.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. BAE is a straight line. Find ∠x.
items.e: BAE is a straight line, so ∠DAB = 180° − 72° = 108°. ∠x and ∠DAB lie between the parallel sides, so ∠x = 180° − 108° = 72°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x + ∠y.
ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠x and ∠BCD are on side BC, between the parallel sides, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 128° = 52°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. DCE is a straight line. Find ∠x.
items.e: DCE is a straight line, so ∠BCD = 180° − 66° = 114°. ∠x and ∠BCD lie between the parallel sides, so ∠x = 180° − 114° = 66°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠ADC and ∠x lie between the parallel sides AB and DC, on side AD, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 118° = 62°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠ABC and ∠x lie between the parallel sides, on side BC, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 63° = 117°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠DAB and ∠x lie between the parallel sides AB and DC, on side AD. They add up to 180°: ∠x = 180° − 68° = 112°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠x and ∠DAB lie between the parallel sides, on side AD: ∠x = 180° − 70° = 110°. Check: 70° + 55° + 125° + 110° = 360°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AD ∥ BC. Find ∠x.
items.e: Here the parallel sides are AD and BC. ∠DAB and ∠x are on side AB, between them, so they add up to 180°. ∠x = 180° − 116° = 64°.

items.q: A trapezium has 2 right angles. One of its other angles is 58°. Find the fourth angle.
Can a trapezium have exactly 3 right angles?
c: No, it has no right angles
Yes, if one side is longer
items.e: 3 × 90° = 270°, so the 4th angle is 360° − 270° = 90°. With 4 right angles the figure is a rectangle, which has 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is not a trapezium.

items.q: WXYZ is a trapezium. WX ∥ ZY. ∠W is 3 times as large as ∠Z. Find ∠W.
items.e: ∠W and ∠Z are on side WZ, between the parallel sides, so they add up to 180°. 4 units = 180°, 1 unit = 45°. ∠W = 3 units = 135°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. ABE is a straight line. Find ∠x.
items.e: ABE is a straight line, so ∠ABC = 180° − 49° = 131°. ∠x and ∠ABC lie between the parallel sides, so ∠x = 180° − 131° = 49°.

sets.title: Figures with triangles and word problems

items.q: From the side, the roof of a bus shelter is a trapezium with parallel top and bottom. Both bottom angles are 62°. Find the sum of the two top angles.
items.e: Each top angle is 180° − 62° = 118° (between the parallel sides). 118° + 118° = 236°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠x.
items.e: CB = CD, so triangle BCD is isosceles: ∠CDB = 35°. ∠BCD = 180° − 35° − 35° = 110°. ∠x is opposite ∠BCD, so ∠x = 110°.

items.q: A floor tile at the void deck is a rhombus. One of its angles is 58°. Find the largest angle of the tile.
items.e: Angles next to each other in a rhombus add up to 180°: 180° − 58° = 122°.

items.q: Ali cuts a rhombus card along the diagonal that joins its two 110° angles. What are the angles of each triangle?
items.e: The cut splits each 110° angle into 55° and 55°. The third angle of each triangle is the other angle of the rhombus: 180° − 110° = 70°. Check: 55° + 55° + 70° = 180°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: In triangle ABC, ∠ABC = 180° − 42° − 31° = 107°. ∠x is opposite ∠ABC, so ∠x = 107°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. E is on DC and BE = BC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠ABC = 180° − 65° = 115° (between the parallel sides). Triangle BCE is isosceles, so ∠BEC = 65° and ∠EBC = 180° − 65° − 65° = 50°. ∠x = 115° − 50° = 65°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. E is on AB. Find ∠x.
ABCD is a parallelogram. AEB is a straight line. Find ∠x.
items.e: In triangle ADE, ∠AED = 180° − 66° − 54° = 60°. AEB is a straight line, so ∠x = 180° − 60° = 120°.

items.q: Hui Min bends a 60 cm wire to make a parallelogram. One side is 18 cm. How long is a side next to it?
items.e: Opposite sides are equal: 18 + 18 = 36 cm. The other two sides share 60 − 36 = 24 cm, so each is 12 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
Mr Tan’s plot in the community garden is a parallelogram. One angle is 4 times as large as the angle next to it. Find the smaller angle.
items.e: Angles next to each other add up to 180°. 5 units = 180°, 1 unit = 180° ÷ 5 = 36°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠x.
items.e: AB = AD, so triangle ABD is isosceles and ∠x = ∠ADB. ∠x = (180° − 64°) ÷ 2 = 58°.

items.q: The top of a study table is a trapezium. Two of its angles are at the ends of a slanted side, between the parallel sides. One is 50° more than the other. Find the larger angle.
items.e: The two angles add up to 180°. 2 units = 180° − 50° = 130°, 1 unit = 65°. Larger angle = 65° + 50° = 115°.

items.q: Raju draws parallelogram PQRS and joins the diagonal PR. ∠SPR = 35° and ∠PRS = 40°. Find ∠PQR.
items.e: In triangle PRS, ∠PSR = 180° − 35° − 40° = 105°. ∠PQR is opposite ∠PSR, so ∠PQR = 105°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠ADC = 180° − 76° = 104° (between the parallel sides). In triangle ABD, ∠ADB = 180° − 76° − 40° = 64°. ∠x = 104° − 64° = 40°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. E is on DC and AD = DE. Find ∠x.
items.e: AD = DE, so triangle ADE is isosceles and ∠x = ∠DEA. ∠x = (180° − 112°) ÷ 2 = 68° ÷ 2 = 34°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. E is on DC and AD = DE. Find ∠x.
items.e: ∠ADE = 180° − 70° = 110° (next to ∠A). Triangle ADE is isosceles: ∠DEA = (180° − 110°) ÷ 2 = 35°. DEC is a straight line, so ∠x = 180° − 35° = 145°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium. AB ∥ DC. E is on DC and BE = BC. Find ∠x.
items.e: BE = BC, so triangle BCE is isosceles: ∠BEC = ∠BCE = 70°. ∠x = 180° − 70° − 70° = 40°.

items.q: Zhi Hao measures a quadrilateral. Its angles are 75°, 105°, 75° and 105°, and its sides are 6 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm, in order. What is its best name?
items.e: Opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal, so it is a parallelogram. The sides are not all equal (not a rhombus) and there are no right angles (not a rectangle).
